subject: africanElephant
pitch:
Category: Animal.
Subject: adult African bush elephant.
Style: low-poly.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a low-poly African bush elephant module, working through realistic proportions like shoulder height, body length, and tusk size before structuring the build with the SDK.

With coordinates set (elephant facing +Z, feet at y=0), I'm designing the skeleton: a hips root joint feeding into a spine chain that curves up through the shoulders and neck toward the head, keeping the joint hierarchy simple so chains skin correctly. Then I'm laying out the body itself as a loft following station points roughly tracing the spine but sitting lower, so the mesh skins naturally onto the bone chain.

Now I'm working out the neck and head placement—keeping the neck short with the head carried low, positioning the skull center forward and angled slightly downward from the last spine joint.

I'm sketching the head shape as a scaled, low-poly sphere with a forehead dome, then adding a jaw joint beneath the trunk base and planning the trunk as a chain hanging down roughly two meters with a slight forward curl at the tip.

I'm giving the trunk a "tentacle" role with about six joints, tapering its radius along its length, and planning wrinkle rings using a painted sine pattern to create darker creases instead of separate geometry.

Now I'm working out how to orient small torus ridge pieces along the trunk's sweep frames, matching the torus's default Z-axis to each frame's tangent direction so the rings sit correctly along the surface.

I'm sketching the trunk's path as a series of control points curving down and forward from the base, keeping the lowest point above ground, with the tip curling slightly upward near the end.

I'll give the tip small finger-like spikes to mimic the dual-lip shape, plus a dark flattened sphere for the nostril facing forward. Then I'm setting up the trunk as a catmull-rom chain parented to the head joint, and starting to define curved tusk sweeps emerging from sockets near the trunk base.

For the tusks, I'm plotting a bezier curve that dips down then sweeps forward and upward to mimic African elephant tusk shape, using ivory coloring with a tapered pointed cap and a slightly darker base ring.

For segment length, roughly summing to 1.7 units matches the intended exposed tusk length well. I'm checking clearance against the trunk's radius at different heights to make sure the tusk emerges naturally beside the trunk rather than clipping through it.

Now I'm moving to the ears, planning to extrude a large Africa-shaped outline attached to the side of the head, positioned to give that distinctive broad, sideways-facing ear profile.

Working out the orientation vectors for the ear plane...

Working out the ear's outline coordinates to capture that wide-top, tapering-lower African shape, roughly 1.4m wide by 1.6m tall, with slight smoothing and a thickness taper from 0.06 down to 0.03.

Now I'm checking the ear placement against the body's shoulder width -- placing it attached near x=0.45, y=3.0, z=2.0, angled outward enough to clear the shoulder's half-width of 0.95 so it doesn't overlap the body mesh.

I compute the normal via cross product to get the outward-forward facing direction, then plan how to paint the ear with mottled skin tones, darker rim shading, and distinct inner-face coloring based on surface normal direction.

Now I'm moving to the legs, picturing thick pillar-like columns for an elephant's limbs.

For each leg I'm defining joint points — shoulder, elbow, wrist, foot — and sweeping a tapered radius from thick at the top to narrower at the ankle, then capping with a flat cylindrical foot that sinks slightly and has small toenail boxes ringed around the front.

Still defining joint chains...

I'm deciding on flat shading for the legs to get that faceted low-poly look, while checking whether loft accepts the same sides/smooth options as sweep since it's just a shorthand wrapper.

Now I'm designing the skin paint function — a mottled grey-brown base using noise, with dustier tan tones lower on the legs to mimic dust-bathed elephant hide, and starting to add wrinkle crease details.

I should double check that noise, mix, smoothstep, and paint are all re-exported from the package's main index so my import statement will actually resolve.

Now I'm sketching out texture ideas: a small elephant eye SVG with amber ring and wrinkled lids as a head decal, a nail texture with ridges for the toenails, and a veined ear-inner SVG applied as a decal on the ear surface, figuring out the right direction axis for that decal placement.

For the right ear (s=-1), redoing the cross product gives the opposite orientation: the thickness axis points toward the head and backward, so the front face normal flips sign relative to the left ear's convention — just mirror the computed direction for the decal placement.

Now I'm working out the decal direction and placement: the dir vector is [s*0.8, 0, 0.6] with up along y, positioned at the ear's center computed from the local axis offset. For the vein texture, I'm planning a branching pattern from the root edge with a pinkish blotchy patch, keeping alpha at or above 0.5 so it doesn't get cut by the opacity threshold.

For the remaining details, I'm sketching bristle-card textures for a tail tuft (dark coarse hairs at the tip of a four-joint chain tail), sparse bristle cards scattered on the forehead and back for the elephant's coarse body hair, and deciding to keep toenails as simple flat-colored boxes rather than textured, possibly adding a separate eye texture.

Now I'm planning wrinkle decals: pale transparent arc-line textures applied at the knees, neck folds, and around the eyes, using dark stroked lines with partial opacity. I'm figuring out the decal placement and orientation on each leg sweep so the wrinkle faces forward at the knee joints, applying this to all four knees plus the neck and eye areas.

I'll skip toenails and mud splatter for now. For tusks, I'm planning a color gradient along the tube from ivory tip to stained brown base, and considering how to build the skull as a scaled sphere positioned near the trunk base with asymmetric radii to shape the head, then placing the eyes on that skull surface using angular coordinates.

I'm working through proportions for the elephant's head and body alignment, adjusting the crown height, forehead dome, and neck/body junction so the skull reads as tall and domed relative to the shoulders, and figuring out how the chest front and rounded cap at the body's front edge should meet the head.

I'm reconsidering body length by adjusting the end stations' widths and heights so the rounded caps at front and back don't overlap the head or extend too far, then checking total head-body length against a real elephant's roughly 6-meter proportions and tweaking the rump station position to lengthen it slightly.

Now I'm positioning the legs relative to the body outline, making sure the rear leg sits within the body's cross-section at that z-coordinate. I'm also designing the lower jaw as a separate tapered box beneath the trunk base, parented to the head joint, and placing the trunk's emergence point on the face so it starts just inside the skull's front contour before adding a forehead bump.

Then I'm working out the eye placement using spherical coordinates around the head center, positioning them on the sides of the face with a slight downward tilt and applying a small dark decal texture for the eyes.

I'll add a brow wrinkle decal above the eye, plus a small dark temporal gland streak stuck onto the surface between eye and ear as a cheap flattened sphere detail.

For the tail, I'm working out a hanging chain of points from the rump down to the body's rear cap, trying to estimate where the cap surface actually sits so the tail attaches naturally rather than floating or clipping -- using a ray cast against the body surface to find the right starting point.

I'm sketching the tail path points relative to the rump root, aiming for roughly 1.5 meters of length ending near the hocks, and planning tuft cards at the tip frames.

Still writing frame math...

Setting cross:true so the tuft reads from every side, and giving cards a bone reference to the tail's last joint so they stay rigid. I'll leave the flow and lean defaults mostly alone since the facing axis already handles the orientation.

Writing bristle texture SVG...

Now for trunk wrinkles, I'm using paint hiding with sinusoidal ring creases based on the chain's sweep coordinate, darkening the surface where the ring pattern peaks to simulate bark folds.

For ridges along the trunk, I'm sweeping low-poly toruses along the trunk's chain at regular intervals, using the tangent at each point to orient the rings and give the silhouette subtle bumps.

Still figuring out the frame parameter...

The ring is rigidly skinned to the bone while the trunk has smooth skinning, so they won't bend perfectly together, but that's acceptable at rest. I'm working out the trunk's radius taper function along the parameter t, roughly blending from 0.3 at the base to 0.095 at the tip with a bit of non-linearity.

For the tip, I'm planning to add small spike details—a finger-like protrusion and maybe a lip shape—placed near the trunk's endpoint with directions angled forward and slightly up to suggest the trunk's natural curve.

For nostrils, I'm positioning two small dark discs near the trunk tip, offset outward along the tangent direction at the end of the path, sized so they sit flush against the rounded dome cap without poking through.

Now I'm mapping out the trunk curve's control points, defining the sequence of positions the trunk path bends through from its base up to the curled tip.

The tip rises slightly forward, and checking the minimum height confirms it stays above the ground with margin to spare. I'm then verifying the trunk's starting point sits properly embedded within the skull ellipsoid's front surface, computing the ellipsoid boundary at that height to confirm the trunk origin is tucked inside rather than poking through.

I want to add a small rounded bulge between the forehead and trunk root to smooth the transition, using a scaled sphere positioned there. For the head I'm keeping cheeks, brow, and upper lip details simple, and noting the skull overlaps the body near the neck joint slightly but that's acceptable.

For the skeleton naming, I'm deciding how to split the spine chain versus a separate short neck chain connecting the last spine joint to the head.

Now I'm working out the neck and head joint hierarchy: splitting the spine into a chain ending near the shoulders, then adding a two-joint neck chain parented to the last spine joint, with the head and jaw joints parented further up the chain with specific positions and aim directions for the hinge.

I'm reconsidering the body loft bone list since it needs to span from hips through spine to neck, and worrying about a degenerate zero-length segment if the hips joint sits at the same location as the spine's start—so I'm repositioning the hips joint separately to avoid that overlap.

I'll go with a bone list of hips, spine, and neck for the body loft, mirroring the tail chain's separate treatment, and now I'm checking how the loft path's z and y coordinates project across the joint positions to verify alignment.

I'm laying out spine and neck joint coordinates, then considering adding a subtle spine ridge using small flattened cones placed via surface raycasts along the body at intervals from the rear to the shoulders.

Now I'm thinking through pelvis protrusions and shoulder blade bumps using the same raycast approach, plus adding wrinkle decals along both flanks projected onto the body surface.

Modeling the elephant's feet as rounded cylinders positioned at the base of each leg, sinking slightly into the floor for realism, and arranging nail boxes in an arc around the front of each foot with varying counts for front versus hind feet.

The foot attaches to the tip joint of the leg chain, which with 3 named joints resolves to joints[2]. I'm sweeping the chain along the leg path with smooth skinning, defining a radius function that tapers over the parameter t.

Checking the leg proportions: legs sit outward from the body center with enough spacing between left and right, so the chosen radii won't make the legs overlap or collide with the torso.

I'll add a blending ellipsoid sphere at the leg top to smooth the shoulder-to-body transition, and keep using the same skin paint consistently across legs, body, and spheres.

For the head, I'm using scaled sphere geometries for the skull plus cheek and jaw details. For the mouth, I'll draw a thin dark sweep under the trunk base for the lip line and use a tapered frustum box for the lower jaw, both painted in the skin color since the pink interior won't be visible.

I'm adding a pale pink lower lip tint as a small box cap, then a short darker cylinder ring at each tusk socket to represent the base sleeve. For the ears, I'm setting up hinge-joint bones parented to the head, extruding the ear mesh on each joint, and aiming the joint direction upward so the default local-X roll works as the hinge axis.

I'm placing the ear root near the head's upper side and tuning the outline's vertical range so the ear top sits near the head crown (~3.55) and the tip hangs down to about 1.7, matching an African elephant's proportions, while widening the outline slightly for the ear's far edge.

Checking the geometry, the ear's lower-middle point extends past the body's half-width and slightly overlaps where the front leg sits, so I'm comparing the ear's x-position against the leg's outer radius at that height to see if they clash.

Since the clearance is marginal, I'm adjusting the ear's splay direction to angle it outward and forward a bit more, redefining the ear's orientation axis and front-face normal vectors to get better separation from the leg while keeping the decal placement consistent with the new angle.

Now I'm figuring out the decal placement offset relative to the ear root, and considering how the asymmetric vein texture needs to mirror correctly depending on which side (left/right) the ear is on, since the root should always face toward the head regardless of mirroring.

Still working through the cross product...

So for s=-1, ex evaluates to the negative of that vector, meaning the right side of the drawing actually corresponds to -ex, placing that root on the right — which suggests the mirroring convention means s=-1 puts the root on the left side instead.

For the left ear (s=1), the root toward the head sits on the viewer's left side, matching the drawing's unmirrored root-left orientation—so no mirroring needed there. That confirms mirroring applies specifically when s is negative.

Eye drawings seem symmetrical enough to use the same mirroring convention regardless of sign. Now I'm setting up the eye dimensions and SVG viewport, along with the color palette—skin tones, dark accents, ivory, nail color, and pink—plus planning body wrinkle textures using paint-based creases, aiming for a part count above 180.

Tallying components: body loft, hip and shoulder bulges, ridge cones, pelvis bumps, leg sweeps and feet, toenails split between front (4-5) and hind (3-4) counts, head pieces like skull, trunk root, cheeks, brow, jaw and mouth, eye decals and socket details, trunk rings and fingers, nostrils, and tusks with sleeves—building toward the full part inventory needed for the model.

Now adding ears with rims and decals, tail sprout with tuft cards and tip bulb, bristle cards for head/back/chin, body wrinkle decals, and paint-based details like dust patches and mud splatter on the legs. I'm estimating around 100 parts so far against a 180-340 target, so I'm layering in more: toe nail details, ankle fold rings (three torus rings per leg for twelve total), neck wrinkle ridges, and eyelash details to round out the realism.

I'm now sketching draped crease lines along the body using surface-draping curves for skin folds behind the shoulder and in front of the thigh — a few arcs per side with dark coloring and subtle lift, being cautious that the sample points stay near the body surface so the drape function doesn't fail.

Checking bounding constraints next: feet sit at y=0, trunk tip and tail stay above ground, tusks and ears fit within the expected height range. I'm finalizing rig roles too — legs get contact points, tail and trunk get their own chain roles, ears act as hinges, and spine/neck get named chains.

Starting to write the actual code now...

Still blending crease and highlight colors...

Checking that the descending smoothstep for mud works correctly with reversed edges, then moving on to the trunk paint logic.

I'm defining a trunk coloring function that samples the base hide color, then layers ring patterns using sine waves and smoothstep blending to add bark-like streaks and highlights.

Now I'm moving to the ear paint function, blending in darker tones at the rim and mottled pink-grey noise across the interior to simulate texture and veining.

For the tusk, I'm layering an ivory base with subtle grain noise, a darker stain near the base, and lighter worn coloring near the tip, following the tusk's path parameter.

Now I'm starting the SVG for the eye, drawing the eyelid shape in dark skin tone before adding the eye ellipse itself.

Writing SVG code...

I'll switch to fully opaque dark brown for safety, using color #463f3a, and work out scaling so stroke widths stay visible at the target canvas size. For the ear veins, I'm sketching a pink wash shape sized to the ear's proportions, rooted at the left center.

For the pink patch, I'm drawing a semi-transparent blob with branching vein strokes in a darker rose tone, keeping edges hard for the low-poly look. For the bristle shapes, I'm defining tapered strand paths in dark brown.

Checking pixel density: at a 128px sprite with a 64-unit viewbox, that's 2px per unit, so a 6-unit strand base becomes 12px — plenty, though tips tapering below 3px get trimmed.

For the nail, I'll use a flat solid color. Now moving to the builder setup for the African bush elephant, I'm weighing paint resolution — texel density math suggests roughly 9mm per texel at 1024, which is tight for fine 3cm creases, so bumping paintSize to 2048 for crisper detail while keeping the atlas at 4096.

I'm building the body loft with sections at hips, spine, and neck, defining width/height at each point along the body with faceted 12-sided cross-sections for that elephant hide look. Now I'm shaping the skull using a sphere geometry scaled and flattened for faceted shading, bound to the head bone.

Next I'm placing the eyes by sampling the skull's surface geometry at angular positions and elevations, then projecting decals onto those hit points with proper orientation vectors so the eye markings face outward correctly on each side.

Adding small gland and brow details...

Adding a trunk base wedge shape, then considering a mouth line along the jaw — maybe skip the sweep curve and just rely on the jaw box, with small dark mouth-corner marks placed near the lower face.

Still defining jaw geometry...

I should double-check the tail attachment at the rump sprout point, adding a guard in case that reference comes back null.

Still plotting tail points...

Still writing tail tuft code...

Scattering sparse bristle cards across the forehead and back using seeded randomization to keep placement deterministic but natural-looking.

Now I'm adding spine ridge cones that raycast downward along the back to place small bony bumps at intervals, plus hip bone bumps raycast from above at angled offsets.

For the body creases, I'm sweeping thin tubes along catmull-rom paths down each side near the shoulder/leg junction to create drape folds, checking whether the fold position actually clears the leg geometry at that z-depth.

I'm repositioning the shoulder fold to z=0.55 so it sits behind the leg rather than buried inside it, and similarly adjusting the thigh fold near the hind leg to z=-0.6 for visibility. Now I'm figuring out where to place knee decals, which requires locating the front surface of each leg at the knee joint.

For front legs I need wrist-wrinkle decals around y≈0.7 facing forward, and for hind legs front-knee decals using a forward direction vector—keeping decal sizes smaller than the leg diameter so the curved wrinkle lines project cleanly onto the surface. I'm also setting up ankle ring details along the leg chain.

Working out torus radius...

I'll keep the leg radius tapering linear, going from front radius 0.44→0.31 and hind 0.48→0.31. For knee bumps, I'll skip separate kneecap spheres and instead stick small scaled spheres onto the hind legs only by raycasting onto the leg sweep surface.

Now for the foot: I'm placing a flattened cylinder at the ankle joint sized so its bottom sits exactly on the ground plane, matching the leg's taper radius. I'll add nail boxes positioned around the front half of the foot using angle-based offsets for placement.

Naming the joints: front legs get "shoulderL/elbowL/handL" style, hind legs "hipL/kneeL/footL", with the tip being the paw joint for each three-point chain.

Setting coordinates for each leg's joint positions, parenting front legs to the spine's last joint and hind legs to the hips, and adding sphere bulges at the shoulder to blend the leg into the body without poking through the back.

Now I'm defining the rig chain structure with parent/role/contact options, then setting up the head joint direction and ear joint attached to a root point on the skull. I'm working through the ear extrusion parameters, adjusting the thickness tuple so the tip and root taper correctly rather than being reversed.

I'm thinking through how to type the ear outline array, deciding between importing an `OutlinePoint` type, casting as `any`, or inferring types from an inline literal, while marking the tip point as sharp for proper bevel smoothing.

I'm also checking the ear root position against the skull's curvature at that height and depth — the root at x=0.52 ends up poking outside the skull's radius, so I'm adjusting it inward to around x=0.4–0.42 so the ear base sits properly embedded in the head.

Now I'm working out the ear's lowest point relative to the outline bottom to confirm it stays above the jawline, then sketching the ear decal: positioning the earvein texture near the root, projected along an outward-facing direction vector so it wraps the front surface correctly, with size and mirroring handled based on which side of the head it's on.

I'm worried the decal region doesn't fully align with the ear's actual silhouette—some vein vertices could fall outside the ear shape at certain y-values and get clipped or project onto the wrong surface. I'm narrowing the decal bounds to a smaller centered patch so it stays safely within the ear outline across its height.

Still, since those stretched quads are mostly transparent anyway, visible artifacts should be minimal, so I'll keep the decal but decide to also preserve the vein paint layer as a backup rather than dropping it. With the ear detailing settled, I'm moving to assembling the trunk chain and sweep geometry using the chain builder API.

Writing trunk chain code...

I'd rather pass explicit `at` and `bone` fields so the bone resolves to a rigid Joint reference, applying the same ring-torus approach to the legs. For the trunk tip, I'm checking that the last joint in the unnamed six-count chain correctly gives the finger/tip reference.

Now I'm computing the end tangent and position of the trunk path to place two finger spikes at the tip, mimicking an African elephant's dorsal and ventral trunk fingers — offsetting the base up/down slightly and giving each spike its own direction, length, and radius with pinkish skin coloring.

For the tusks, I'm using cubic bezier curves mirrored on each side, swept with a tapered radius and pointed end to form the tusk shape, then checking that the tusk's starting position aligns with the skull surface near the trunk base rather than poking through it.

Adding a darker sleeve ring near the tusk base, positioned along the path's tangent at a small offset to sit just past the gumline.

I'm checking the tusk color mapping uses path position, and confirming tusks stay rigid relative to the head bone, then verifying ear-top height against ground level. Now I'm defining the hips joint as the root spine bone and building out the spine chain with a catmull-rom curve through several points up the torso.

Continuing to build the skeleton, I add a neck chain splitting into two joints, then a head joint parented to the last neck joint, aiming slightly downward-forward to match the neck's final segment. I define a jaw joint parented to the head with its own aim target, and set up the main body loft bone spanning hips, spine, and neck -- noting the loft path doesn't need to fully match the neck chain's extent, and flagging that mixing Joint and Chain types in that bone list could cause trouble.

Now I'm scattering card-based fur elements across the body surface using area-weighted sampling with a minimum distance constraint, sized and leaned for a shaggy look, colored dark brown. I'm also working out wrinkle decals along the flanks, trying to figure out the right surface point and ray direction so the decal projection correctly hits the skin mesh.

I'm settling on a small hand-picked list of 8 wrinkle positions across the thigh and torso area rather than generating them procedurally, deciding to skip neck and eye-socket wrinkles for now, and noting that the surface query method might return null so I need to handle that case in the types.

I'm checking triangle budgets stay within limits -- spheres at 192 tris each, trunk rings around 960, and cards using around 4 flat triangles plus extra per bend segment, with roughly 60 cards total staying comfortably under the 60k cap.

Now I'm starting the actual implementation: setting up the imports, meta info, color palette constants for dark skin, nails, mouth, creases and bristles, then moving into building the eye SVG and textures inside the build function for determinism.

Writing eye SVG code...

Still writing SVG code... I notice the lash strokes extend above the viewBox and clip off, so I need to adjust the viewBox bounds.

Still drawing wrinkle curves...

Still drawing vein paths, now moving on to sketch bristle shapes with tapered curved outlines...

Starting the main builder function, setting up a 2048 paint size with textures, skeleton, and body to follow, and using a shared left/right naming convention for limb generation.

Writing leg-chain logic...

Still writing leg ring code...

For the decal placement, I'm figuring out the front-facing position using surface ray-casting against the leg tube to find the right attachment point.

Still tuning the knee bump geometry...

Now I'm thinking through adding the thigh and shoulder bulge parts, attaching spheres to the first joint of the bone chain with flattened scaling for front versus back legs, then moving on to shaping the tail root.

I'm sprouting the tail from the rump point, building a curved path of displaced points relative to the rump location and letting the sprout function prepend the starting point so I don't duplicate it, then setting knot counts for the tail's curve.

Checking where the rear hit point lands vertically relative to the rump's cap taper -- at y=2.7, roughly 0.55 above the rear station's center, so the cap's elliptical cross-section narrows z there, landing around z=-2.58.

Now I'm computing the tail tuft's end point and spreading a ring of fan frames around it for the tuft cards, then moving on to the wrinkle crease drapes along the body surface using catmull curves swept into thin colored strands.

Writing the second fold curve, checking it clears the hind leg's thigh bulge geometry, then adding ridge sticks by ray-casting down onto the skin surface at intervals along the z-axis and embedding small cone shapes.

I'm skipping chest and chin details for now, scattering small decorative cards across the skull's crown using a filtered random distribution, and adding a forehead wrinkle decal positioned via spherical coordinates with a null guard in case the dome doesn't register a hit.

Rechecking rig evaluation and part/stick options for consistency, confirming the scatter filter uses the hit's normal vector correctly, and verifying the rng seeding pattern matches other scatter calls. I'm now computing the nostril position on the trunk by taking the tangent at the endpoint and offsetting outward along it.

Writing jaw geometry...

Computing the ear root direction vector and deriving the decal attachment point by offsetting along that normal, then sketching the ear's outline shape spanning roughly from y=0.55 down to y=-1.

Setting the decal placement and size parameters, then considering whether to add a separate ear rim extrusion before deciding to skip it and move on to checking type compatibility for the extrude call's direction input. I'm finalizing the hide color mixing function, blending two hex tones by a blend factor to get an interpolated color tuple, then starting to define a tint helper for adjusting that color further.

Working through the paint functions for trunk, ear, and tusk, confirming they read position/normal/scalar inputs without mutating them. I'm also checking that the skull center point accepts a tuple array and setting up the tusk paint sweep along a bezier path with color blending by parameter t.

No extra geometry needed for the neck, and belly shading is already handled by the paint pass. Finalizing the build by returning the root bone, with tail cards relying on automatic frame generation.
